Positive: decriminalisation, no trans-specific offence, Pride events proceed, police hate-crime training, courts enforcing regional court rulings on transcription (rule of law functioning in a protective direction for trans people — the March 2026 case at least).

So the traveller-facing sphere: no documented exposure reaching visitors beyond general social conservatism and hostile rhetoric. Climate signals: anti-discrimination body exists and acts (fining airline, investigating printers) though follow-through limited; courts enforce regional rulings; Constitutional Court struck down gender-identity-studies ban — functioning rule of law in a somewhat protective direction.

Here we have no documented visitor-facing harms at all. 0.75 tier: documented acceptance and operating remedies; here acceptance is not documented — attitudes described as conservative, hostility rising.

So between 0.55 and 0.65. The documented negatives are: hostile official rhetoric (state climate signal), gender identity excluded from hate-crime and anti-discrimination law (thin recourse for trans-specific incidents, though sex-based coverage exists and the council acts), municipal resistance to visibility events, and Pride participants fined. But nothing shows a trans visitor being harmed or refused service or targeted by police. LGB organisations register; the anti-discrimination council does act on LGBT printing refusal — that's recourse operating somewhat.

The visitor's key exposures: hospitality/service refusal? No data. Police ID checks — no data. Medical emergency — LGR gap could cause problems for residents; a visitor uses home passport so less.

I'd put around 0.62–0.66. Given rising hostility, official rhetoric framing gender markers as eroding norms, and trans not covered by hate-crime law (so an attack on a trans visitor may not get aggravated-hate-crime treatment; though assault prosecution still available), the recourse is thinner than the 0.75 examples. I'd land 0.62.

Hmm, consider whether the state rhetoric amounts to "state threat-framing" (tier 1 / rule 19c). The PM opposing identity-document amendments and mocking marker changes, candidates "against LGBTQ" — this is hostility expressed in rhetoric, not in operational rules applied to visitors (no facility exclusion, no custody rule). So it's climate, weighty but not tier 1.

I'll give 0.62.
